summary: Max Walleser worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (PhD c. 1900–1902), later serving at Heidelberg University as Privatdozent (1911) and associate professor for Indian philology (1918–1936).

Max Weber was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Heidelberg, Strasbourg, Berlin, and Göttingen, he held academic posts at Freiburg (c. 1894–1896), Heidelberg (c. 1896–1903), Vienna (c. 1918), and Munich (c. 1919–1920).
Maximilian Bittner was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna under Friedrich Müller from around 1887 to 1890.
Maximilian Enger worked in Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn by 1851 and served there as a Privatdozent from 1852 to 1861.

Maximilian Hoth works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hamburg (2023–2025) and studied at the Göttingen Academy, becoming a PhD candidate at the University of Munich in 2026.
May Oung worked in the field of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1904 to 1907.

Historian Maya Jasanoff studied at Harvard College, the University of Cambridge, and Yale University (c. 1997–2002). She held posts at the University of Virginia (c. 2003–2009) and Harvard University, where she was appointed professor in 2009.
Maya Keller-Grimm worked in Buddhist studies. She served as leader of the Altbuddhistische Gemeinde from circa 1946 to 1989 and was an editor of Yāna between circa 1954 and 1989.
Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a General Council member there from 1964 to 1965.

Mayumi Nasu works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Nasu held posts as a lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) and as a specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Małgorzata Sulich-Cowley works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. She studied at Pune, Lausanne, and the University of Warsaw (PhD 2013), later working as a teaching associate at SWPS University (2015) and research assistant at Warsaw (2018–2021).
McComas Taylor works in Indology. He earned a PhD from the Australian National University, where he held the post of Emeritus Professor in 2005.

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Harvard and Chicago under Clyde Kluckhohn. He completed his PhD in 1955 and served as professor at the University of Chicago from 1955 to 1998.

Md Mohiuddin Ahmed Tanvir earned a BA in Buddhist and religious studies from the University of Dhaka (2019–2023). He held counsellor posts at AHZ Bangladesh (2024–2025), IDP Education (2025–2026), and Kampus Group (2026).

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Sri Jayewardenepura, Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing (PhD c. 2003). He served as Senior Lecturer at the University of Colombo around 2003.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University (2002–2010) and served as an associate professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (attested 2017).
Megumu Honda was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Johannes Rahder, Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells, and later served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).

Mei Ching Hsuan specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at the University of Bonn, studying under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh, and served as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Meiji Yamada is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He also served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1971 and 2007).
